# Layer kinds

What a composition's `layers` can hold. `turbomotion comp catalogue` prints the same data as JSON.

## `solid`

A flat rectangle: backgrounds, flashes, mattes. Size defaults to the composition.

```json
{
  "color": "#101828",
  "type": "solid"
}
```

## `text`

Text with real shaping. `font` is a family or a file; `align` left|center|right (the layer's pos is the alignment edge, vertically centred); `width` wraps. Characters the designed font does not have take a fallback face and are painted in the same colour as the rest of the line. `preset` is a named per-character animation (see `text_presets`); `animators` build your own (GSAP staggers or After Effects range selectors). `text` can also be a counter {from, to, at, dur, ease, decimals, sep, prefix, suffix}. Animator props include per-character 3D (`z`, `rotation_x|y|z`, `scale_z`, seen through `perspective`), `fill_hue|saturation|brightness` and `stroke_width`; an animator's `cipher` {charset, rate, seed, settle} decodes noise into the real characters. Animator `props` are DELTAS added to each character's rest state: `opacity: -1` hides it, a positive opacity changes nothing (rest is already full), `scale: -1` shrinks it to nothing. A `selector` {start, end, offset, shape, smooth, random} gives weight 1 to the characters whose place along the text (0 to 1) lies between `start + offset` and `end + offset`, so a window that never reaches a character leaves the text untouched: animate `offset` (for example {from: -0.2, to: 1, dur: 2}) to sweep a window along the line. `check` warns (animator-never-applies, animator-opacity-delta) when an animator can change nothing. `path` {an ellipse/points/d/... geometry or a `layer` id, reverse, perpendicular, force_align, first_margin, last_margin, travel} sets the text along a path (`travel` 0..1 is one exact lap of a closed path); `surface` {kind: cylinder|sphere, radius, turn, back} wraps it on a drum or ball; `marquee` {speed, gap, repeat} scrolls a seamless row; `outline_only` with `stroke_trim` [start, end] draws the glyph outlines on. `box` {fit: "text", padding, radius, fill, min_width, align, per_line} draws a rectangle behind the glyphs that is as wide as the characters showing (see `text_box`).

```json
{
  "align": "center",
  "color": "#ffffff",
  "font": "Avenir Next",
  "mark": {
    "at": 1.0,
    "word": "move"
  },
  "pos": [
    960,
    540
  ],
  "preset": {
    "at": 0.3,
    "name": "reveal"
  },
  "role": "title",
  "text": "Make it move\nlike you mean it",
  "type": "text",
  "weight": 800
}
```

## `image`

Your own picture. `fit` cover|contain|fill|none, `focus` keeps the subject when cropping, `camera` is a Ken Burns move {from: {zoom, center}, to, ease}, `parallax` {depth: <grey image, white = near>, strength} gives a 2.5D move. `sampling` nearest|linear overrides automatic cubic enlargement / mipmapped reduction. EXIF orientation is applied. Size the source to at least the pixels shown (check warns about upscaling).

```json
{
  "camera": {
    "ease": "sine.inOut",
    "from": {
      "center": [
        0.45,
        0.5
      ],
      "zoom": 1.0
    },
    "to": {
      "center": [
        0.6,
        0.5
      ],
      "zoom": 1.3
    }
  },
  "fit": "cover",
  "focus": [
    0.6,
    0.5
  ],
  "src": "photo.jpg",
  "type": "image"
}
```

## `video`

A video file streamed through ffmpeg. `src_in` starts into the file, `speed`, `loop`, `fit`, `size`; its sound is mixed unless `mute`. Combine with masks and mattes for rounded or shaped clips.

```json
{
  "loop": true,
  "mute": true,
  "size": [
    640,
    360
  ],
  "src": "clip.mp4",
  "type": "video"
}
```

## `audio`

A sound on the timeline: `volume` (a property), `fade_in`, `fade_out`, `src_in`, `speed`. Mixed in Rust (soft-clipped) and muxed into the render. Other layers can react: `amp("id")` is its loudness, `onset("id")` spikes on hits.

```json
{
  "fade_out": 1.0,
  "id": "music",
  "src": "music.wav",
  "type": "audio",
  "volume": 0.8
}
```

## `mesh`

A solid: a triangle mesh from a `geometry` generator, lit by the composition's lights (ambient, point, spot, directional; `material` sets specular and shininess) and drawn through its camera. Needs "three_d": true. Geometry kinds: `text` (glyph outlines extruded, with an optional chamfer; one layer per letter to stagger a word), `box`, `sphere`, `torus`, `cylinder` (`top: 0` makes a cone) and `extrude` (an SVG path pushed into depth). It turns about its own middle, so `rotation` tumbles or spins it (`"rotation": [0, "time*90", 0]` is a turntable). `color` is the front and a curved skin, `side` the walls, `back` the back; `side` defaults to a darkened `color`.

```json
{
  "color": "#e8402f",
  "geometry": {
    "bevel": 6,
    "depth": 60,
    "font": "Avenir Next",
    "kind": "text",
    "size": 300,
    "text": "M",
    "weight": 800
  },
  "material": {
    "shininess": 40,
    "specular": 0.8
  },
  "pos": [
    960,
    540,
    0
  ],
  "rotation": [
    20,
    {
      "dur": 0.8,
      "ease": "back.out(1.4)",
      "from": -90,
      "to": 0
    },
    0
  ],
  "side": "#8a2017",
  "three_d": true,
  "type": "mesh"
}
```

## `shape`

Vector shapes with fill, gradient, stroke, dashes, trim (draw-on), morph and repeat. Geometry: rect, ellipse, polygon, star, d (SVG path), points. A fill is a colour or a gradient (linear {from, to}, radial {center, radius}). Every item animates its own properties (`trim`, `rotation`, `scale`, `opacity`, rect/ellipse sizes); `anchor` is the item's pivot for rotation and scale, in the item's own units from the shape's origin. `taper` thins the stroke toward its ends (see `stroke_taper`); an item's `repeat` takes a `palette` (see `palette_cycle`).

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "fill": {
        "gradient": {
          "from": [
            0,
            -120
          ],
          "stops": [
            [
              0,
              "#ff8a00"
            ],
            [
              1,
              "#e52e71"
            ]
          ],
          "to": [
            0,
            120
          ],
          "type": "linear"
        }
      },
      "radius": 24,
      "rect": [
        -200,
        -120,
        400,
        240
      ]
    },
    {
      "ellipse": [
        0,
        0,
        90,
        90
      ],
      "stroke": {
        "cap": "round",
        "color": "#ffffff",
        "width": 8
      },
      "trim": {
        "end": {
          "at": 0.3,
          "dur": 1,
          "ease": "power3.inOut",
          "from": 0,
          "to": 1
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "ellipse": [
        300,
        0,
        160,
        160
      ],
      "fill": {
        "gradient": {
          "center": [
            0,
            0
          ],
          "radius": 90,
          "stops": [
            [
              0,
              "#ffe9a8"
            ],
            [
              0.6,
              "#ff8a00"
            ],
            [
              1,
              "#e52e71"
            ]
          ],
          "type": "radial"
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "anchor": [
        60,
        20
      ],
      "fill": "#8be9fd",
      "rect": [
        -60,
        200,
        120,
        40
      ],
      "rotation": {
        "dur": 1.2,
        "ease": "sine.inOut",
        "from": -20,
        "to": 20
      }
    }
  ],
  "pos": [
    960,
    540
  ],
  "type": "shape"
}
```

## `null`

An invisible transform to parent other layers to: one handle moves, scales or shakes a whole group.

```json
{
  "id": "rig",
  "pos": [
    960,
    540
  ],
  "rotation": {
    "dur": 2,
    "ease": "sine.inOut",
    "from": -4,
    "to": 4
  },
  "type": "null"
}
```

## `precomp`

Plays a nested composition from `comps` as one layer, with its own clock (offset, speed, time remap, loop). `sampling` nearest|linear controls transformed pixels (default linear); use nearest for integer-scaled pixel art. Everything a layer can do (effects, masks, mattes, 3D) works on it.

```json
{
  "comp": "inner",
  "pos": [
    960,
    540
  ],
  "scale": {
    "dur": 0.6,
    "ease": "expo.out",
    "from": 0.8,
    "to": 1
  },
  "speed": 1,
  "start": 0.5,
  "type": "precomp"
}
```

## `adjustment`

Applies its effects to everything below it (a grade, a glitch, a blur over the whole picture). Masks limit it to a region; opacity fades it.

```json
{
  "fx": [
    {
      "amount": 4,
      "effect": "chromatic_aberration"
    },
    {
      "effect": "vignette",
      "strength": 0.4
    }
  ],
  "type": "adjustment"
}
```

## `texture`

Paints a generator shader over the layer (noise, clouds, cells, stripes, grid, gradient, aura (a soft multi-point mesh-gradient backdrop with animatable point positions and colours), light_leak, bokeh, floor, or your own `effects/<name>.sksl` with `@kind generator`). Use it as a background, a matte, or blended over footage. `comp fx list` shows each one's parameters.

```json
{
  "blend": "screen",
  "opacity": 0.6,
  "params": {
    "high": "#9aa7c7",
    "scale": 300
  },
  "shader": "clouds",
  "type": "texture"
}
```

## `particles`

A particle system where every particle is a closed-form function of its age (so any frame renders alone). The emitter sits at the layer's position. Emit continuously (`rate`) and/or in `burst`s; `prewarm` starts it already running. Shapes: soft, circle, square, spark (streak along travel), star, ring, or your own outline `{"path": {"d": "M0 -1 L1 1 L-1 1 Z"}}` (any path geometry, fitted to the particle's size and turned by its spin: a snowflake, a leaf). Use blend `add` or `screen` for light.

```json
{
  "angle": -90,
  "blend": "add",
  "colors": [
    [
      0,
      "#ffffff"
    ],
    [
      0.4,
      "#ffd36b"
    ],
    [
      1,
      "#ff4a3d"
    ]
  ],
  "drag": 0.4,
  "gravity": [
    0,
    160
  ],
  "life": [
    1,
    2.5
  ],
  "opacity_over_life": [
    [
      0,
      1
    ],
    [
      0.8,
      1
    ],
    [
      1,
      0
    ]
  ],
  "pos": [
    960,
    900
  ],
  "rate": 90,
  "shape": "spark",
  "size": [
    4,
    10
  ],
  "speed": [
    180,
    420
  ],
  "spread": 40,
  "trail": 3,
  "type": "particles"
}
```

## `pack`

Graphics owned by another crate and registered by the host (a globe, a map, a chart): {"type": "pack", "name": "<pack>", "params": {...}}. `comp catalogue` lists the packs this build has under `packs`. A pack paints a picture from its params and the layer's time; everything else (transform, effects, masks, mattes, 3D) works on it like any layer.

```json
{
  "color": "#000",
  "type": "solid"
}
```

## `camera`

A 3D camera (the topmost active one is used). Layers with "three_d": true are projected through it. Default: 1:1 at z = 0.

```json
{
  "poi": [
    960,
    540,
    0
  ],
  "pos": [
    {
      "dur": 4,
      "ease": "sine.inOut",
      "from": 760,
      "to": 1160
    },
    540,
    -1800
  ],
  "type": "camera",
  "zoom": 1800
}
```

## `light`

A light for 3D layers: ambient, point, directional or spot. 3D layers are shaded by every active light.

```json
{
  "color": "#ffd9a0",
  "intensity": 1.2,
  "kind": "point",
  "pos": [
    400,
    200,
    -500
  ],
  "radius": 1400,
  "type": "light"
}
```

## `extrude`

Depth for a three_d text, shape or solid layer: copies stepping back in z, coloured from `color` to `far`. Show it with a camera move or a Y Rotation. `fx` apply to the front face only; the slices behind it stay plain colour, so an outline ring lies over the first slices and hides the sides at shallow angles.

```json
{
  "align": "center",
  "color": "#ffd166",
  "extrude": {
    "color": "#e8590c",
    "depth": 60,
    "far": "#c2410c"
  },
  "pos": [
    960,
    540
  ],
  "rotation": [
    0,
    18,
    0
  ],
  "size": 220,
  "text": "88888",
  "three_d": true,
  "type": "text",
  "weight": 800
}
```

## `box` (a text layer key)

A filled rectangle fitted to a text layer's characters, drawn behind the glyphs inside the same layer: it moves, scales, turns, fades and takes the layer's effects with the text, in either `effect_space`. It is as wide as the characters showing plus the padding on both sides and as tall as the lines it covers (ascent to descent) plus the padding above and below, measured from the real shaped text (kerning, tracking, line breaks, the font's own metrics). It follows what is showing: a typewriter bar grows with every character, a masked rise grows as the line comes out from behind its mask, a tracking-in widens it, and a text with nothing showing has no box. Whitespace has no extent, so a box hugs the first and last visible character of a line. The same measurement is `source_rect_at_time(t, include_extents)` in the engine, the `bounds` of the layer's `content` in `comp inspect`, and `bounds` in the SDK's `measure()`.

* `align`: Which side of a box widened by `min_width` keeps its place: "left" grows to the right, "right" to the left, "center" both ways (default: the text layer's own `align`).
* `fill`: Required: the box's colour (a colour, a palette name or an animated colour).
* `fit`: Required: "text", the only choice. The box is fitted to the measured characters.
* `min_width`: The box is never narrower than this many pixels, padding included (default 0).
* `padding`: [x, y] pixels between the characters and the box: x on the left and right, y above and below. Each is a property (a number, an expression, {from, to, at, dur, ease} or keys), so it can animate; neither may be negative (default [0, 0]).
* `per_line`: true draws one box for each line that has characters showing, each as wide as its own line; false (default) draws one box round the whole block.
* `radius`: Corner radius in pixels, held to half the box's shorter side, so a large one makes a pill (default 0).

```json
{
  "bg": "#10141f",
  "dur": 3,
  "fps": 30,
  "height": 1080,
  "layers": [
    {
      "box": {
        "fill": "#e63946",
        "fit": "text",
        "min_width": 360,
        "padding": [
          {
            "at": 0.2,
            "dur": 1.4,
            "ease": "power2.out",
            "from": 56,
            "to": 36
          },
          24
        ],
        "radius": 28
      },
      "color": "#ffffff",
      "font": "Avenir Next",
      "id": "typed",
      "pos": [
        300,
        400
      ],
      "preset": {
        "at": 0.2,
        "dur": 1.4,
        "name": "typewriter"
      },
      "size": 96,
      "text": "Make it move",
      "type": "text",
      "weight": 800
    },
    {
      "box": {
        "fill": "#e2c48a",
        "fit": "text",
        "padding": [
          28,
          14
        ],
        "per_line": true,
        "radius": 10
      },
      "color": "#10141f",
      "font": "Avenir Next",
      "id": "lines",
      "pos": [
        300,
        700
      ],
      "size": 64,
      "text": "Two lines,\nEach with its own bar",
      "type": "text",
      "weight": 700
    }
  ],
  "width": 1920
}
```

## `palette` (a repeater key)

A repeater can give every copy its own colour from a palette. Add `palette`, `cycle` and `paint` to a layer `repeat` (the original is copy 0, the others 1 to count - 1) or to a shape item's `repeat` (copy 0 is the item itself). Both repeaters read the same three keys. Copy i falls `i + offset` colours along the palette: `step` takes colour `floor(i + offset) mod n` (a whole offset moves every copy on by that many colours, a fractional one holds the colour until it reaches the next whole number, a negative one moves back); `gradient` blends the two colours either side of `(i + offset) mod n`, the last colour blending back into the first, in the film's working colour space (display-encoded values in an ordinary film, light in a `linear_light` film, so it matches a Skia gradient drawn in the same film); `ping_pong` runs the palette forwards then backwards, `0 1 .. n-1 n-2 .. 1 0 1 ..`, the end colours not doubled. `reverse` reads the palette from its last colour to its first before any of this. `offset` is a property (a number, an expression, {from, to, at, dur, ease} or keys), so it can animate: animate it from 0 to n over a loop to run the colours along the row. The colours in `palette` may be animated too. `paint` says which paint of a copy takes the colour: "fill" (default; for text and solid layers their own colour), "stroke" or "both". A shape item takes a fill colour only when its fill is one flat colour (a gradient or metal fill is refused, with `paint: "stroke"` available), and a stroke only when it has one. A layer repeater works on text, solid and shape layers (an image or a precomp has no colour to replace, and is refused when the film is planned); each copy carries the result as a `swatch` {palette, index, cycle, paint}, a layer key you can also write by hand. The per-copy `opacity` of the repeater applies to the coloured copy as before. The repeater has whole copies only: `count` and `copies` are integers, so there is no fractional copy to colour.

* `cycle`: {mode, offset, reverse}. `mode` is "step" (default), "gradient" or "ping_pong". `offset` is how many colours the palette is shifted on, a property that may animate and may be negative or fractional (default 0). `reverse` reads the palette last colour first (default false).
* `paint`: "fill" (default), "stroke" or "both": which paint of the copy takes the colour.
* `palette`: Required to colour copies: a list of at least one colour (hex, a palette name, an animated colour). Written inside `repeat`.

```json
{
  "bg": "#10141f",
  "dur": 3,
  "fps": 30,
  "height": 1080,
  "layers": [
    {
      "color": "#ffffff",
      "id": "chip",
      "pos": [
        260,
        340
      ],
      "repeat": {
        "count": 8,
        "cycle": {
          "mode": "step",
          "offset": {
            "dur": 3,
            "ease": "none",
            "from": 0,
            "to": 4
          }
        },
        "offset": [
          200,
          0
        ],
        "palette": [
          "#e63946",
          "#f1fa8c",
          "#2a9d8f",
          "#264653"
        ]
      },
      "size": [
        150,
        150
      ],
      "type": "solid"
    },
    {
      "id": "ramp",
      "items": [
        {
          "ellipse": [
            260,
            720,
            70,
            70
          ],
          "fill": "#ffffff",
          "repeat": {
            "copies": 8,
            "cycle": {
              "mode": "gradient",
              "offset": 0.5
            },
            "offset": [
              200,
              0
            ],
            "opacity": 0.9,
            "paint": "both",
            "palette": [
              "#e63946",
              "#2a9d8f",
              "#9b5de5"
            ]
          },
          "stroke": {
            "color": "#ffffff",
            "width": 8
          }
        }
      ],
      "pos": [
        0,
        0
      ],
      "type": "shape"
    }
  ],
  "width": 1920
}
```

## `taper` (a shape item key)

`taper` on a shape item makes its stroke thinner toward either end of the outline: a variable-width stroke. It is drawn as the filled region between the two offset curves of the path (with the stroke's own `cap` and `join`; corners are joined, tight bends do not leave holes, and the edges stay within a fiftieth of a pixel of the true offset curve). `start` is the first point of the outline and `end` the last. Each end has a `length` (how far from the end the stroke takes to reach its full width) and a `width` (how wide it is at the end itself, default 0: a point). A length is pixels, or `{"fraction": f}` of the outline's length; a width is pixels, or `{"fraction": f}` of the stroke's `width`; each is a property that may animate. A length cannot be negative and is held to half the outline, so the two ends never overlap: a taper of 5000 px on a 400 px path is 200 px at each end and the stroke is full width at the middle only. `ease` (a GSAP name, default linear) shapes the width from the tip to the full width and is the same at both ends, measured from each tip. Between the tapers the stroke is its full `width`. A closed outline is tapered from its start point: `start` runs along the first stretch and `end` back along the last stretch before the start point, so with both given the stroke pinches at the start point from both sides, and with only one the stroke steps from the tip's width to full there. Several contours (a path with more than one `M`) are each tapered along their own length. A tapered stroke follows the trimmed outline: with `trim`, the taper is measured along the part that is drawn. The item needs a `stroke` and cannot be dashed; the colour, opacity, `cap` and `join` are the stroke's; a repeater's palette colours it like any stroke.

* `ease`: A GSAP ease (default linear): how the width rises from the tip to the full width, measured from each tip.
* `end`: {length, width}: the taper at the last point of the outline (on a closed outline, the stretch before the start point).
* `length`: Pixels, or {"fraction": f} of the outline's length: how far from the end the stroke takes to reach its full width. 0 or more; held to half the outline.
* `start`: {length, width}: the taper at the first point of the outline.
* `width`: Pixels, or {"fraction": f} of the stroke's width: how wide the stroke is at the end itself (default 0). 0 or more.

```json
{
  "bg": "#10141f",
  "dur": 3,
  "fps": 30,
  "height": 1080,
  "layers": [
    {
      "id": "arrow",
      "items": [
        {
          "d": "M 260 800 C 560 300 1060 1000 1560 380",
          "stroke": {
            "cap": "round",
            "color": "#e63946",
            "join": "round",
            "width": 56
          },
          "taper": {
            "ease": "power2.out",
            "end": {
              "length": {
                "fraction": 0.12
              },
              "width": {
                "fraction": 0.3
              }
            },
            "start": {
              "length": 360,
              "width": 0
            }
          },
          "trim": {
            "end": {
              "dur": 1.5,
              "ease": "power2.inOut",
              "from": 0,
              "to": 1
            }
          }
        },
        {
          "ellipse": [
            1560,
            380,
            150,
            150
          ],
          "stroke": {
            "color": "#f1fa8c",
            "width": 36
          },
          "taper": {
            "end": {
              "length": 120
            },
            "start": {
              "length": 120
            }
          }
        }
      ],
      "type": "shape"
    }
  ],
  "width": 1920
}
```

## `motion_blur` (a composition key)

True motion blur, as After Effects has it: the frame at time `t` is the whole scene (every layer's transform, its motion path and keys with their ease or speed and influence handles, the camera, 3D layers, text animators, particles, effects and masks) drawn at several moments while the shutter is open and averaged. The shutter is open over `[t + phase, t + phase + angle]`, both in degrees of the frame interval (360 degrees is one frame), so the default angle of 180 and phase of -90 blur over a quarter of a frame either side of `t`. Only layers with `"mblur": true` blur. The blur is an average of finished pictures in the film's working colour, so with `color.linear_light` it averages light (an edge half through a pixel is level 188 on screen, not 128), and it averages premultiplied pictures, so alpha coverage is exact. Samples are spread evenly over the shutter (the middle of each of `samples` equal slices) and their number is fixed: the smear of a fast mover is `samples` copies, so it steps when the distance between samples (travel / samples) is more than a pixel or two; lower the angle or raise `samples` (at most 16; each sample draws every blurred layer again). A layer that does not move, and has no effect, matte or clip, is drawn once and exactly as without blur. A comp with the block and no switched layer costs nothing. Only the layers of the root composition have a switch: a precomp layer with `"mblur": true` blurs everything it shows, whatever is switched inside it, and a switch inside a nested composition does nothing (`comp check` says so).

* `mblur`: A layer key, not part of the block: `"mblur": true` switches motion blur on for the layer (default false). With no `motion_blur` block the older key's shutter is used.
* `older key`: `"mblur": {"samples": 8, "shutter": 180}` on the composition (and on a timeline) is kept as it always was: the shutter is centred on the frame time whatever its angle, a layer that is not showing at the frame time takes no part, and the numbers are not range-checked. Use `motion_blur` for After Effects' phase and for a layer that enters or leaves during the shutter; the two keys together are an error.
* `samples`: Moments averaged per frame, 2 to 16 (default 16). A frame costs about this many times a frame without blur, for the layers that blur.
* `shutter_angle`: How long the shutter is open, in degrees of the frame interval, 0 to 720 (default 180). 0 draws no blur. A 100 px per frame mover blurs over 100 * angle / 360 px plus its own size.
* `shutter_phase`: When the shutter opens relative to the frame time, in degrees of the frame interval, -360 to 360 (default -90: a 180 degree shutter centred on the frame time; 0 opens it at the frame time, so the smear trails ahead of the layer).

```json
{
  "bg": "#101820",
  "dur": 2,
  "fps": 30,
  "height": 720,
  "layers": [
    {
      "color": "#ffd166",
      "id": "puck",
      "mblur": true,
      "pos": {
        "keys": [
          {
            "ease_out": {
              "influence": 60,
              "speed": 0
            },
            "t": 0,
            "v": [
              320,
              360
            ]
          },
          {
            "ease_in": {
              "influence": 60,
              "speed": 0
            },
            "t": 1.2,
            "v": [
              960,
              360
            ]
          }
        ]
      },
      "rotation": {
        "at": 0,
        "dur": 1.2,
        "ease": "power1.inOut",
        "from": 0,
        "to": 180
      },
      "size": [
        120,
        120
      ],
      "type": "solid"
    },
    {
      "align": "center",
      "color": "#f4f7ff",
      "pos": [
        640,
        600
      ],
      "size": 56,
      "text": "SHUTTER 180",
      "type": "text"
    }
  ],
  "motion_blur": {
    "samples": 16,
    "shutter_angle": 180,
    "shutter_phase": -90
  },
  "width": 1280
}
```
